EfficiencyCorrelation

This is a byte-for-byte preserved upstream teaching notebook from an external university curriculum (retained under its original open license; see Third-Party Notices and the folder README). Rendered below for convenient reading on the web alongside the downloadable original .ipynb.

⬇ Download Original Notebook (EfficiencyCorrelation.ipynb) 📖 Folder Overview & Provenance 🗂 All Repository Materials
Python · Executable Cell 1
import numpy
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
%matplotlib inline

def efficiency(X):
    return 1./numpy.trace((numpy.linalg.inv(X.T.dot(X))))
Python · Executable Cell 2
corrs=numpy.arange(-0.9,1.0,0.1)
eff=numpy.zeros(len(corrs))
for i in range(len(corrs)):
    c=corrs[i]
    data=numpy.random.multivariate_normal([0,0],
                            [[1,c],[c,1]],100)
    eff[i]=efficiency(data)
Python · Executable Cell 3
plt.plot(corrs,eff)
plt.xlabel('correlation')
plt.ylabel('efficiency')
